This document covers how the course runs day to day. It is not the syllabus. The
official course syllabus is published through NC State's Class Search tool and
is also posted in Moodle. Where the two documents overlap, the syllabus governs.

## Instructors and Communication

**Corey T. White, PhD**, Center for Geospatial Analytics
ctwhite@ncsu.edu, office hours by appointment

**Teaching Assistant: [name]**
[unity id]@ncsu.edu, office hours [day, time, location]

Use the Moodle forum for anything about assignments, software, or data, since
the answer usually helps more than one person. Use email for anything personal
or time sensitive. Expect a reply within [one business day] on weekdays. Put
GIS584 in the subject line.

Distance education students can meet with the instructor or TA over Zoom during
the same office hours as on-campus students. Ask and a link will be sent.

## Course Website and Moodle

The course website at
<https://ncsu-geoforall-lab.github.io/gis-584-uas-course/> holds the schedule,
lecture slides, topic pages, assignments, and data links. The site is built with
Quarto and Reveal.js, the source is at
<https://github.com/ncsu-geoforall-lab/gis-584-uas-course>, and the material is
licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

Moodle holds the course forum, assignment submissions, project material, and
grades: [Moodle]({{< var course_params.moodle_link >}}).

## Lectures

Lectures cover principles, theory, concepts, and methods, and are mostly
software independent. Slides and video for each topic are linked from that
topic's page, reachable through the course schedule or through Moodle. Topic
pages also link to additional reading.

Lecture recordings are posted to [Panopto]({{< var course_params.panopto_link >}})
and linked from each topic's pages. Distance education students work from the
same recordings and the same topic pages as the on-campus section.

## Assignments

Most topics include a hands-on assignment, linked from that topic's page on the
course website.

For each topic you submit a report of at least two pages, including images and
tables, with these sections:

- **Introduction:** the task and the problem
- **Methods:** general description of the methods and concepts used
- **Results:** the results, including maps, graphs, and tables, with comments
- **Discussion:** anything unexpected or problematic in the results, any issues
  with the methodology or software, and suggestions for improvement
- **Conclusion:** one or two sentences on what you learned

Submit through Moodle as a PDF using the naming convention
`LastnameFirstname_HW#.pdf`.

Reports are due [day of week] at [time] following the schedule on the course
website. Late reports lose 10% per week or part of a week, with no credit after
two weeks. If something comes up, tell me before the deadline rather than after.

Extra credit is given for innovative solutions, creative problem solving, and
extensions to the assigned tasks. Show the extension clearly in the report so it
can be found.

## Semester Project

The project is a complete UAS analysis workflow applied to a problem you choose,
from acquisition through interpretation, presented in your portfolio. It is
worth 40% of the course grade.

Milestones:

- Project proposal, due [date]
- In-progress presentation, [date]
- Final report and portfolio, due [date]

Milestones are hard deadlines and are not accepted late. The proposal and the
presentation exist so you get feedback while there is still time to act on it,
which a late submission cannot deliver. If you are going to miss one, contact me
before the date.

Project requirements and the rubric are on the Projects page of the course
website.

All course work is collected in an electronic portfolio that accumulates across
your GIS courses.

## Software

- [GRASS {{< var software.grass.version >}}]({{< var software.grass.website >}}), installation instructions at
  <https://ncsu-geoforall-lab.github.io/geospatial-modeling-course/logistics.html#software>
- [Agisoft Metashape]({{< var software.agisoft.website >}}), licensed by

- [OpenDroneMap](http://opendronemap.org/) and WebODM

Additional tools referenced in the course, not required:
[PDAL](https://pdal.io/en/stable/) for point cloud processing,
[LAStools](https://lastools.github.io/) and [libLAS](https://liblas.org/) for
managing LAS files with GRASS, and
[MicMac](https://github.com/micmacIGN/micmac) as an alternative structure from
motion package.

## Computational Resources

NC State students can reserve an environment in the [Virtual Computing Lab
(VCL)](https://vcl.ncsu.edu/). Use the `Agisoft Metashape & GRASS GIS - Ubuntu`
image. VCL is the fallback if your own machine cannot handle a processing job,
and it is available to distance education students on the same terms as
on-campus students.

[Add WebODM server access details here once the CGA instance is provisioned.]

If a processing run fails or takes an unreasonable amount of time, post the log
to the forum rather than restarting it repeatedly.

## Data

Course datasets are hosted publicly and linked from the topic pages and below.
Download data before class rather than during it.

### GRASS Projects

- [GRASS North Carolina dataset](https://grass.osgeo.org/sampledata/north_carolina/nc_spm_08_grass7.zip)

### Ground Control Points (Mid Pines)

12 GCPs taken at Mid Pines:

- [GRASS pack]({{< var data.gcp_12_decimal_pack_url >}})
- [GeoJSON]({{< var data.gcp_12_degrees_url >}})

### Processed data

- [LakeWheeler_NCspm]({{< var data.lake_wheeler_url >}}) Mid Pines project with a timeseries of DSMs from 2015 flights
- [Smaller sample point cloud: 2015_06_sample_points_NCsmp.las]({{< var data.mid_pines_2015_las_url >}})

### Lidar data

- [Classified lidar point cloud in LAS format for Mid Pines]({{< var data.mid_pines_lidar_url >}})
- [Secref and Mid Pines interpolated DEM/DSM (use r.unpack)]({{< var data.secref_mid_pines_spm_elev >}})

### Orthoimagery

Orthophotos as GRASS packed rasters; use r.unpack from within the LakeWheeler_NCspm
project to import them, with -o to override the projection (HARN versus NAD83 datum,
the difference is negligible).

- [Nov 2015 (pack)]({{< var data.lake_wheeler_flight_Nov_2015_orthos >}})
- [Mar 2017 (pack)]({{< var data.lake_wheeler_flight_Mar_2017_orthos >}})
- [Jun 2017 (pack)]({{< var data.lake_wheeler_flight_Jun_2017_orthos >}})
- [Jul 2024 (COG)]({{< var data.lake_wheeler_flight_July_17_2024_orthophoto >}})

## Flight Operations and Field Safety

Flight planning and execution are taught in Topic 3. Students are not required
to hold a Part 107 remote pilot certificate to complete the course, and
assignments can be completed with provided imagery or in simulation.

Any student who does fly is responsible for operating under [FAA Part
107](https://www.faa.gov/uas/commercial_operators/become_a_drone_pilot),
including airspace authorization, visual line of sight, and altitude limits, and
for following NC State policy on UAS operations on university property. Do not
fly over people, do not fly a course exercise you have not planned in writing,
and do not fly alone.

## Attendance

Attendance is recorded at each meeting of the on-campus section and does not
carry points toward your grade. University definitions of excused absences are
in [REG
02.20.03](https://policies.ncsu.edu/regulation/reg-02-20-03-attendance-regulations/).
Tell me in advance when you can.

## Academic Integrity

Students are bound by the [Code of Student
Conduct](https://policies.ncsu.edu/policy/pol-11-35-01/). Discussing approaches
with classmates is encouraged. Submitting someone else's processing results,
figures, or text as your own is not. When you use code, a workflow, or a dataset
you did not create, cite it.

More information: [Student Conduct](https://studentconduct.dasa.ncsu.edu/) and
[NC State Policies, Regulations, and Rules](https://policies.ncsu.edu/).

## Use of Large Language Models

Large language models may be used for assignments and projects. Cite the use,
including which model and what you used it for, in the methods section of your
report. Uncited use is an academic integrity violation. LLMs may not be used on
exams.

An LLM will produce confident, wrong GRASS syntax and confident, wrong
photogrammetry advice. Check what it gives you against the documentation, and
remember that you are responsible for what you submit.

## Accommodations

Reasonable accommodations are made for students with documented disabilities.
Register with the [Disability Resource
Office](https://dso.dasa.ncsu.edu/) and provide the accommodation letter as
early in the semester as possible so arrangements can be made. See [REG
02.20.01](https://policies.ncsu.edu/regulation/reg-02-20-01/).

If any part of the course website, slides, or data is not accessible to you,
tell me and it will be fixed.
